samples.summary: Remote-change clear drops the image selection but leaves an in-flight resize drag armed on a now-stale (blockId, offset)
samples.evidence: The new `editor.clearImageSelection()` in `store.onRemoteChange` (docs-view.tsx:392) routes to `clearImageSelectionForMutation` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1295-1299), which only does `selectedImage = null; render()`. It does NOT call `abortImageResizeDrag()`. That helper's own doc comment (editor.ts:2578-2591) states the invariant: "every path that clears the image selection because the offsets moved under it has to drop the drag too, or the next `mouseup` commits the drag's size onto whatever inline now sits at that coordinate." A remote peer's edit is precisely the mutation that can land *while the mouse button is still down*, unlike undo/redo/reset (editor.ts:2115, 2151, 3958) which all do abort the drag. After such a remote edit, `imageResizeDrag` keeps its mousedown-captured `{blockId, offset}` and the document-level mousemove/mouseup listeners stay installed; on mouseup `handleImageResizeMouseUp` (editor.ts:2554-2572) does `doc.findBlock(blockId)` + `findImageAtOffset(block, offset)` and, if *any* image now sits at that shifted offset, writes the dragged width/height onto it via `doc.applyInlineStyle` — resizing the wrong image and pushing that to the CRDT. This is the exact failure mode the unconditional clear was added to prevent, only half-fixed.

samples.summary: Unconditional clear adds a second full render per remote change when an image is selected
samples.evidence: `clearImageSelectionForMutation` calls `render()` when a selection existed, and `onRemoteChange` renders again at line 406 after `refresh()`/cursor restore. With an image selected, every remote keystroke from a peer now paints twice (once against the pre-refresh document). Cosmetic/perf only; the comment at 388-391 acknowledges the ordering intent.

samples.summary: In read-only, Ctrl+H (find-and-replace request) opens a bar identical to plain find, with no feedback that replace is unavailable
samples.evidence: `editor.onFindReplaceRequest` (docs-view.tsx:443-446) still sets `findBarShowReplace(true)` for viewers, but `{showReplace && !readOnly && ...}` renders nothing, so the shortcut silently appears to do the same thing as Ctrl+F. Behavioral rough edge rather than a defect; the gate itself is correct.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. docs-view.tsx:392 calls editor.clearImageSelection(), which is aliased to clearImageSelectionForMutation (editor.ts:3845); that helper (editor.ts:1295-1299) only nulls `selectedImage` and renders — it never calls abortImageResizeDrag(). abortImageResizeDrag (editor.ts:2592-2598) is the only thing that removes the document-level mousemove/mouseup listeners installed at mousedown (editor.ts:2654-2655), and it is called only from undo (2115), redo (2151), the commit path (2535) and resetAfterDocumentReplace (3958) — never from the remote path. Remote changes fire unconditionally (yorkie-doc-store.ts:576-581) with no drag suppression, so a peer edit arriving while the button is down leaves `imageResizeDrag` armed on a now-stale {blockId, offset}; handleImageResizeMouseUp (editor.ts:2527-2575) then re-resolves that coordinate with findBlock/findImageAtOffset and, if any image occupies it, writes the dragged width/height via doc.applyInlineStyle onto the wrong image and pushes it to the CRDT. The helper's own doc comment (2581-2585) names this exact invariant, and undo/redo/reset all honour it, confirming the remote path is the omission. Real and blocking under the correctness lens (wrong state written to the shared document on a reachable collaborative race).
